blogs.title: Sepsis, DIC, and the TMA Switch: Recognizing CM-HUS When the Dust Settles
blogs.description: Early in fulminant sepsis, coagulopathy and organ failure can obscure an evolving thrombotic microangiopathy. This post walks through how to distinguish DIC from a superimposed CM-HUS as the inflammatory storm calms—rising LDH, falling haptoglobin, persistent thrombocytopenia, and new schistocytes despite improving infection. We’ll cover using the smear early, applying PLASMIC and ADAMTS13 to triage TTP, and why normal coagulation studies later in the course should pivot your differential toward TMA.

blogs.title: Eculizumab After Bacteremia: A Practical Playbook for Infection-Triggered CM-HUS
blogs.description: How do you time complement blockade when TMA follows a recent bloodstream infection? This piece lays out a stepwise approach: stabilize sepsis, initiate PEX as a bridge while excluding TTP, confirm culture clearance, then start eculizumab promptly to preserve renal recovery. It details vaccine strategy (MenACWY and MenB), antibiotic prophylaxis while vaccine immunity develops, counseling about residual invasive disease risk despite vaccination, and practical monitoring once on therapy.

blogs.title: The Dog-Bite Pathogen You Can’t Miss: Capnocytophaga canimorsus in the ED and ICU
blogs.description: Capnocytophaga canimorsus can turn a minor dog bite into fulminant sepsis with leukopenia, DIC, and multiorgan failure—even in immunocompetent adults. We review bedside clues, empiric antibiotic choices that cover beta-lactamase–producing strains (e.g., piperacillin–tazobactam or amoxicillin–clavulanate), and why diagnosis often lags due to slow culture growth, prompting consideration of rapid molecular methods. We also highlight complications like ischemic digits and hypoglycemia, and discuss de-escalation once susceptibilities return.

blogs.title: Needles in a Storm: When and How a Kidney Biopsy Clarifies TMA
blogs.description: In dialysis-dependent AKI with suspected TMA, kidney biopsy can confirm the diagnosis, stage injury, and refine prognosis. This post reviews safety thresholds (platelets generally >50–75×10⁹/L and corrected coagulopathy), peri-procedural planning in patients recently on anticoagulation or PEX, and the key histologic signatures of TMA versus isolated ATN. We discuss how biopsy results influence urgency for complement blockade and expectations for renal recovery.

blogs.title: Don’t Trust the C3: Making Sense of Complement Studies and Genetics in CM-HUS
blogs.description: Normal C3/C4 levels do not exclude CM-HUS, and treatment timing can confound interpretation of functional assays. We unpack which tests to send before therapy when possible, why AH50 may be low after eculizumab or PEX, and how to avoid over-calling ‘consumption.’ The post also summarizes genetic testing yield, counseling when results are negative, and how genotype and clinical severity shape decisions on duration of complement inhibition.

blogs.title: When a Positive Coombs Misleads: Drug-Related DAT Positivity vs MAHA
blogs.description: A positive DAT in a septic patient with anemia and thrombocytopenia can misdirect clinicians toward autoimmune hemolysis. We examine causes of false-positive DAT (penicillins, recent transfusions), red flags for MAHA (schistocytes, marked LDH rise, low haptoglobin, paradoxically poor reticulocyte response), and why steroids won’t fix a TMA. Learn a pragmatic algorithm to pivot quickly from suspected AIHA to a TMA workup and life-saving therapies.
